title: A Pack of Gum Changed Every Store in America
fb_caption: Every beep at the checkout goes back to one pack of gum. Those black bars are a 12-digit number in stripes, a red laser reads it, and in most cases the price isn't in the barcode at all: the store's computer looks the number up. The first real checkout scan happened on June 26, 1974, at a Marsh supermarket in Troy, Ohio, on a 10-pack of Juicy Fruit gum. Self-checkout or a cashier?
engagement_comment: Self-checkout or a cashier? 1 = self-checkout every time, 2 = a cashier, please, 3 = whichever line is shorter.

beats.text: Every beep at the checkout goes back to one pack of gum.
Those black bars aren't a picture. They're a twelve-digit number, written in stripes a machine can read.
The scanner sweeps a red laser across the stripes and reads that number back.
Here's what most people miss. The price usually isn't in the barcode. The store's computer looks the number up and sends the price back.

overlays.text: THE PRICE ISN'T IN THE BARS

beats.text: The very first scan at a real checkout was June 26, 1974, at a Marsh supermarket in Troy, Ohio. The item: a ten-pack of Juicy Fruit gum.
Now that same idea is on almost everything you buy.
Self-checkout or a cashier? Tell us below.
